title: With Putin overextended in Ukraine, Armenia is turning away from Russia
gist: With Russia overextended in Ukraine, Armenia is dismantling Russian control (arms, border posts, rail, gas) and pivoting to the US, India and the EU; the US-brokered Armenia-Azerbaijan deal and the 74% US-owned TRIPP corridor would graft Armenia onto the Russia-bypassing Middle Corridor, pending an Armenian constitutional change on Karabakh.

insights.claim: Russia supplied at least 94% of Armenian arms imports in 2011-2020, but India replaced Russia as Armenia's largest defense supplier in 2025 with contracts exceeding $1.5 billion.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Indian defense exporters are gaining share in former Russian markets.
insights.locator: Moscow’s leverage is now in decline.

insights.claim: Russian assets in Armenia remain extensive: Gazprom owns the gas distribution network, Russian Railways runs the rail system under a concession to 2038, and the Gyumri base with about 3,000 troops is chartered to 2044.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Watch for concession terminations or asset disputes affecting Russian state companies' foreign holdings.

insights.claim: Pashinyan is moving to end the Russian rail concession, and Armenia's parliament passed a 2025 law opening a path to EU accession; Armenian border guards took over the airport in 2024 and the Iranian crossing in January 2025.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Concrete institutional steps signal durable westward realignment.

insights.claim: Russia's capacity to police its near abroad is being consumed by the war in Ukraine, so Moscow could not stop US outreach to Armenia.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Russian overextension creates openings for Western commercial and strategic entry across the former USSR.
insights.quote: The capacity Moscow once used to police its periphery is being consumed in Ukraine.
insights.locator: Russia has been unable to stop

insights.claim: Russia's historic method in its neighbourhood has been to lay a political 'mine' in a neighbour's territory (Abkhazia, South Ossetia, Transnistria, Crimea, Karabakh) and then present itself as the only power able to defuse it.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Useful lens for assessing frozen-conflict risk in post-Soviet states.
insights.locator: Russia’s method of control in the so-called near abroad

insights.claim: JD Vance visited Yerevan in February with a civil nuclear agreement and an $11 million drone package; in May Marco Rubio signed a strategic partnership charter, critical minerals memorandum and a framework for a US-developed transit corridor.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Opens Armenian civil nuclear and critical minerals to US firms.

insights.claim: The US-led Armenia-Azerbaijan peace deal includes the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP), 74% held by Washington, linking Azerbaijan to Turkey across Armenia and joining Armenia to the 6,500-km Middle Corridor that bypasses Russia.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Middle Corridor logistics, rail and transit infrastructure are beneficiaries; Russian transit routes lose relevance.
insights.locator: The Russian ruler has good reason

insights.claim: Azerbaijan conditions its signature on removing Karabakh-unification language from Armenia's 1990 independence declaration; resolving this would secure TRIPP, open the Turkey border, and give Armenia access to Azerbaijani energy, Central Asian trade routes and a line to Europe.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: The constitutional change is the key catalyst to watch for the corridor proceeding.
insights.locator: One clause stands in the way.

insights.claim: Russia's response has been limited to affordable tools: Sergei Kiriyenko took the Armenia file in spring 2025, a Kremlin-linked network ran info campaigns with over 100 million views in a year, Moscow banned Armenian agricultural exports and threatened gas prices.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Expect continued trade coercion (agri bans, gas pricing) as Armenia's pivot proceeds.

insights.claim: Moscow warned that leaving the Eurasian Economic Union would cost Armenia 14% of its economy, and Putin said EU membership would break down trade with Russia.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Quantifies the economic cost Russia claims for Armenian exit — a risk to Armenian growth during transition.

insights.claim: Despite Russian interference, including an opposition allegedly run by Putin-linked billionaire Samvel Karapetyan, Pashinyan's party won 64 of 105 seats in the summer 2026 elections.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Strong mandate reduces political-reversal risk for Armenia's westward turn.

insights.claim: The US, Europe and others should exploit Moscow's preoccupation with Ukraine to cement changes in the South Caucasus while Putin can do little in practice.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Window for Western investment in the South Caucasus is tied to the duration of the Ukraine war.
